items.title: How fighter pilots stay awake at 9 g
items.summary: How does a fighter pilot stay awake at 9 g? At 5 g, a 2016 study on rats measured the blood pressure in the head falling by about 80 mmHg, to nearly zero. No pressure, no blood to the brain, so the vision goes, then the pilot does. The pilot breathes out hard against a closed throat for 3 to 4 seconds, which squeezes the chest and pushes blood pressure back up. A 2026 review says doing the full straining maneuver right adds about 4 g. The limit for military jets is still about 9 g, and that limit is the pilot, not the plane. items.title: Why dry spaghetti won't break in half
items.summary: Why won't dry spaghetti break in half? Bend a strand until it snaps and you typically get three pieces, sometimes four. A 2005 physics paper from Paris argued that the first crack sends a burst of bending waves down both pieces, which sharpen the curve further along until the strand snaps again. In 2018 a team at MIT got just two pieces by twisting the strand first. items.title: You have only ever seen 59% of the Moon
items.summary: You have only ever seen 59% of the Moon. The Moon spins once in 27.3 days and orbits the Earth once in 27.3 days, so the same side always faces us. A slight rock called libration uncovers a bit more every month. Add it all up and 59% of the surface is visible from Earth. The other 41% never faces us. Idea and structure from Mark Rober's Short "Why the Moon Never Changes". items.title: Why a magnet falls slowly through a copper pipe
items.summary: Why does a magnet fall slowly through a copper pipe? In a plastic pipe it would drop a meter in under half a second. In copper, the falling magnet changes the field inside the metal and pushes currents around, and those currents act like a magnet of their own that pushes against the fall. The faster it moves, the stronger the push back, so it settles into a slow, steady speed. Idea and structure: Veritasium's Short "I call this the 'No, You Don't' Law". #shorts #physics #magnets Idea and structure from Veritasium's Short "I call this the 'No, You Don't' Law" https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2FLq...
